remaining_concerns: The affected small-business onboarding segment remains exposed in the initial rollout.
No completed, reviewed risk-acceptance record explicitly approves continued exposure of that segment.
The policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance; neither is shown in the admissible record.
Rollout controls, rollback capability, monitoring, and small initial percentage do not satisfy the disclosure-policy predicate by themselves.
A caveated certification framing narrows the overclaim but does not cure the unresolved compliance condition.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and cited no new evidence IDs; the response mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and conceded the core deficiency. That narrower framing is more accurate than an overbroad certification claim, but it is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the missing element is not merely disclosure wording or cautionary language. It is an unresolved policy predicate: the admissible record still does not show either exclusion of the affected use case from rollout or reviewed risk acceptance explaining why continued exposure is acceptable. Under the stated policy text, monitoring, rollback, and a 6% rollout can mitigate only if one of those conditions is met. Since neither is shown, the certification claim remains noncompliant on the available evidence.
